newsitem.title: USA: U.S. denies Serb report on Karadzic arrest order.
newsitem.headline: U.S. denies Serb report on Karadzic arrest order.

text.p: The United States on Thursday denied a Bosnian Serb television report that NATO peacekeepers had been ordered to arrest former President Radovan Karadzic and his former army commander Gen. Ratko Mladic as indicted war criminals.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters the report was "absolutely and unequivocally false." He said there had been no change in the orders to NATO peacekeeping forces on their behaviour towards alleged war criminals.
The report, quoting unidentified Bosnian Serb security sources, said Karadzic and Mladic were to be arrested on sight and U.S. and British military units had been designated to capture them.

"That report is false, absolutely and unequivocally false. There has been no change in the instructions for (the NATO-led peacekeeping force) pertaining to the detaining and arrest of indicted war criminals," Burns told a regular State Department news briefing.

He said the rule remained that if any of those troops "encounter people who they know to be indicted war criminals they are to detain them for transfer to civilian authority so they may be arrested and then turned over to The Hague for prosecution."
A NATO spokesman in Sarajevo also denied the Bosnian Serb report.

Karadzic and Mladic were indicted during the 1992-95 Bosnian war but no serious effort has been made to arrest them despite repeated pledges by Western powers that they would be put before the United Nations war crimes tribunal in The Hague.
